exposure: Type of ARM: recto-perineal, recto-vestibular, cloaca with native vagina pull-through, cloaca requiring bowel partial vaginal replacement
Anorectal malformations (ARM), including long common channel cloaca and cloacal exstrophy
outcome: Fertility, pregnancy outcomes, mode of delivery
cohort: Female patients with ARM from a single institution database, including patients operated on since 1980.
finding: Women with less complex ARM can achieve spontaneous pregnancy, while those with complex anomalies, particularly requiring bowel partial vaginal replacement, may face infertility and require assisted reproduction.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the most common mode of delivery.
